extraction.name: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes
extraction.description: AMASS is a large and varied database of human motion that unifies 15 different optical marker-based mocap datasets by representing them within a common framework and parameterization. It uses MoSh++ to convert mocap data into realistic 3D human meshes represented by a rigged body model (SMPL). The dataset contains more than 40 hours of motion data, spanning over 346 subjects, and 11451 motions. Each frame includes SMPL 3D shape parameters (16 dimensions), DMPL soft tissue coefficients (8 dimensions), and full SMPL pose parameters (90 dimensions), including hand articulations.
extraction.creator: Naureen Mahmood, Nima Ghorbani, Nikolaus F. Troje, Gerard Pons-Moll, Michael J. Black
extraction.publisher: Meshcapade GmbH; MPI for Intelligent Systems; York University; MPI for Informatics
extraction.citeAs: Mahmood, N., Ghorbani, N., Troje, N. F., Pons-Moll, G., & Black, M. J. (2019). AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes. arXiv:1904.03278.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: AMASS unifies 15 existing optical marker-based motion capture datasets by applying MoSh++ to convert sparse marker data into SMPL body model parameters. For the novel SSM dataset, an OptiTrack mocap system with 24 Prime 17W cameras was used to capture subjects with 67 markers, synchronized with a 3dMD 4D body scanning system (22 pairs of stereo cameras, 22 color cameras, 34 speckle projectors). Subjects wore minimal clothing with markers placed directly on the skin.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Direct measurement, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Markers may get occluded by the body due to pose. If multiple markers of a particular body part are occluded simultaneously, the optimization may result in unreliable and implausible poses. To address missing markers, a coefficient q is introduced that scales the pose prior weight based on the number of missing markers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 15 source mocap datasets: ACCAD, BioMotion Lab (BML), CMU, EKUT, Eyes Japan, HumanEva, KIT, MPI HDM05, MPI Limits, MPI MoSh, SFU, SSM, TCD Hand, TotalCapture, Transitions. Source datasets contain varying markersets ranging from 37 to 91 markers. Publicly available datasets were downloaded from the internet; others were obtained privately or recorded by the authors.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: When hand markers are not present, hand poses are set to the average pose of the MANO model. For the first frame of a sequence, the model is initialized by performing a rigid transformation between estimated and observed markers.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: MoSh++ pipeline with two stages: Stage I estimates body shape and marker locations using 12 randomly chosen mocap frames. Stage II optimizes pose for each frame while keeping shape and marker locations constant. Uses Threshold Acceptance method as an annealing strategy over 4 stages. Varying marker counts are handled with a scaling factor b=46/n.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Results from MoSh++ were manually inspected; problems such as swapped and mislabeled markers were either corrected or held out. A temporal smoothness term is used to help reduce jitter noise in mocap marker data.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: No manual annotation; body shape, pose, and soft-tissue parameters are fit to marker data automatically using the MoSh++ optimization framework with the SMPL body model (with DMPL soft-tissue and MANO hand components).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: MoSh++ (fitting procedure); SMPL body model; SMPL-H; DMPL; MANO hand model; Chumpy auto-differentiation package; Powell's dogleg minimization
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: AMASS is publicly available at http://amass.is.tue.mpg.de. The authors state they will continue to expand the dataset and will support the community in adding new captures as long as they can be similarly shared.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The SSM dataset includes three subjects with varying body shapes. Two of the three subjects were professional models who signed modeling contracts allowing release of their 4D scan data along with synchronized mocap data. Body shape information is recovered for all subjects.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Current runtime of MoSh++ is not real-time. The method does not solve for facial expressions (only body and hands). Given a limited number of mocap markers, allowing more shape variation results in overfitting. The SSM dataset does not currently include captures with articulated hands.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: AMASS is intended for animation, visualization, and generating training data for deep learning in computer vision and machine learning for human motion. Useful for training models of human motion, generating synthetic training data, and texturing/rendering virtual bodies for computer vision tasks.
